title: Oxidation and Reduction
seo_title: Chemistry 12: Oxidation and Reduction Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: oxidation numbers, half-reactions and balancing redox
standard_text: Oxidation and reduction are complementary processes that involve the gain or loss of electrons: oxidation numbers, half-reactions, balancing redox equations, and the reactivity of metals. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 12)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): oxidation numbers, half-reactions and balancing redox. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain.
body_html:
How to think about it

Oxidation is a loss of electrons (oxidation number increases); reduction is a gain of electrons (oxidation number decreases). The substance oxidized is the reducing agent, and the substance reduced is the oxidizing agent.

Redox equations are balanced with half-reactions: balance atoms, then O with H₂O, H with H⁺, and charge with electrons, then make the electrons equal. A table of reduction potentials predicts which reactions are spontaneous.

Example

What is the oxidation number of S in SO₄²⁻?

4 × (−2) + S = −2

Answer: +6

Example

Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu. Which is oxidized?

Which loses electrons?

Answer: Zn

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the oxidizing agent and the substance oxidized.
  • Forgetting to balance charge with electrons.
  • Thinking oxidation always involves oxygen.

items.q: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which is the oxidizing agent?
items.e: CuO gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidizing agent; H₂ is the reducing agent.

items.q: What is the oxidation state of V in VO<sup>2+</sup>?
items.e: Oxygen is −2 (−1 in peroxides), hydrogen +1 (−1 in metal hydrides); the total equals the charge on the species.

items.q: What is the oxidation state of C in C<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup>?
items.e: Oxygen is −2 (−1 in peroxides), hydrogen +1 (−1 in metal hydrides); the total equals the charge on the species.

items.q: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, what is the reducing agent?
items.e: Zinc loses electrons and is oxidized.

items.q: What is reduction?
c: gain of electrons (or a decrease in oxidation number)
items.e: The oxidizing agent is reduced.

items.q: What is the oxidation number of an element in its uncombined state?
items.e: For example, O₂ and Fe have 0.

items.q: What happens when a strip of zinc is placed in copper(II) sulfate solution?
c: copper forms on the zinc and the blue colour fades
the solution turns green and hydrogen forms
items.e: Zinc is more reactive than copper.

items.q: In 2FeCl₃ + H₂S → 2FeCl₂ + 2HCl + S, which is the reducing agent?
items.e: H₂S loses electrons (is oxidized), so it is the reducing agent.

items.q: A piece of copper is placed in lead(II) nitrate solution. Will a displacement reaction occur? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: Yes. Any metal replaces any other metal.
No. Metals never react with solutions.
No. Copper is less active than lead, so no reaction occurs.
Yes. Copper is more active than lead, so it replaces it.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

items.q: What is the oxidation state of C in CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Oxygen is −2 (−1 in peroxides), hydrogen +1 (−1 in metal hydrides); the total equals the charge on the species.

items.q: What is the best oxidizing agent among the halogens?
items.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative.

items.q: In 2FeCl₃ + H₂S → 2FeCl₂ + 2HCl + S, which is the oxidizing agent?
items.e: FeCl₃ (Fe³⁺) gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidizing agent; H₂S is the reducing agent.

No. Magnesium is less active than copper, so no reaction occurs.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

items.q: Why is rusting a redox reaction?
c: iron is oxidized to iron(III) and oxygen is reduced
items.e: Water and oxygen are both needed.

items.q: In 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, which is the oxidizing agent?
items.e: Fe₂O₃ gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidizing agent; Al is the reducing agent.

items.q: Using the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au), which metal is more reactive: zinc or lead?
items.e: Higher in the list = loses electrons more easily.

items.q: A piece of silver is placed in aluminum nitrate solution. Will a displacement reaction occur? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: Yes. Silver is more active than aluminum, so it replaces it.

No. Metals never react with solutions.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

items.q: Which metal will displace copper from copper sulphate solution?
items.e: Zinc is more reactive than copper.

items.q: Why are blocks of magnesium or zinc attached to ship hulls?
c: they corrode instead of the steel hull (sacrificial anodes)
items.e: They are replaced as they wear away.

items.q: How does galvanising protect steel?
c: zinc stops all oxygen reaching the air
zinc reacts with water to make paint
a coating of zinc is oxidized in preference to iron (sacrificial protection)
items.e: Even scratched, the zinc protects.
